ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-02.body:
With $T=12$, the mean is $18$ so the total is $90$. In increasing order $a<b<12<d<e$; to make $e$ as large as possible take $a=1$, $b=2$, $d=13$. Then $e=90-1-2-12-13=62$.

**Answer: 62**

Here $T=12$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-03.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-03.body:
With $T=62$: $162x=124(x+2)-4(2-9x)=124x+248-8+36x=160x+240$. So $2x=240$ and $x=120$.

**Answer: 120**

Here $T=62$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-04.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-04.body:
The cuboid is $60\times40\times30$ cm. Its surface area is $2(60\cdot40+60\cdot30+40\cdot30)=2(2400+1800+1200)=10800$ cm$^2$. $10800/1800=6$ pots.

**Answer: 6**

Here $T=120$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-05.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-05.body:
Let $b$ pupils have both, so $2b$ have neither. Counting: $25+20-b+2b=50$, so $b=5$. Bicycle but not skateboard: $25-5=20$.

**Answer: 20**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-06.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-06.body:
With $T=20$ there are 21 counters. $P=\frac8{21}\times\frac7{20}=\frac{56}{420}=\frac2{15}$. So $p=2$, $q=15$ and $q-3p=9$.

**Answer: 9**

Here $T=20$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-07.body:
$8T=72^\circ$. Triangle $ABD$ is isosceles with apex $72^\circ$, so $\angle ABD=\frac{180-72}2=54^\circ$. Then $\angle DBC=180-54=126^\circ$. Triangle $DBC$ is isosceles with $DB=BC$, so $\angle BCD=\frac{180-126}2=27^\circ$.

**Answer: 27**

Here $T=9$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-08.body:
The $n$th term is $136-8(n-1)=144-8n$. With $T=27$ we need $n=270$: $144-2160=-2016$.

**Answer: -2016**

Here $T=27$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-09.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-09.body:
$\frac{11}4\times\frac{29}6\div\frac{55}8=\frac{11\times29\times8}{4\times6\times55}=\frac{29}{15}$ after cancelling $11$, $8/4=2$ and $2/6=1/3$, leaving $\frac{29}{3\times5}$. So $a=29$, $b=15$ and $2b-a=30-29=1$.

**Answer: 1**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-10.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-10.body:
The cubes have side $\frac12$ cm. The 12 cubes form a closed ring (a $5\times3$ frame), and in a ring each cube touches exactly two others, so there are 12 touching pairs. Faces: $12\times6=72$, minus $2\times12=24$ hidden faces, leaves 48 exposed faces of area $\frac14$ cm$^2$ each: $A=12$ and $\frac A2=6$.

**Answer: 6**

Here $T=1$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-11.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-11.body:
With $T=6$ he mixes 1 part A with 5 parts B. Take each part as 20 units: 20 of A has 5 red and 15 blue; 100 of B has 40 red and 60 blue. Total red $45$, blue $75$, ratio $45:75=3:5$. So $b-a=5-3=2$.

**Answer: 2**

Here $T=6$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-12.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-12.body:
Let Tia be $x$ years old and $T=2$: $x=2(x+2)-2(x-2)=2x+4-2x+4=8$.

**Answer: 8**

Here $T=2$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-14.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-14.body:
With $T=10$: the first part takes $\frac{10}x$ h and the second part (15 km at $\frac x2$) takes $\frac{30}x$ h. So $\frac{40}x=8$ and $x=5$.

**Answer: 5**

Here $T=10$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-15.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-15.body:
With $T=5$: a pentagonal pyramid has 10 edges and 6 vertices; a pentagonal prism has 15 edges and 10 vertices. With $p$ pyramids and $q$ prisms: $10p+15q=70$ and $6p+10q=44$, i.e. $2p+3q=14$ and $3p+5q=22$. Then $6p+9q=42$ and $6p+10q=44$ give $q=2$, $p=4$. Total $6$ shapes.

**Answer: 6**

Here $T=5$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-16.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-shuttle-16.body:
With $T=6$, $4T=24$. Let the pink speed be 100. Blue $=124$. Blue is 20% slower than black: $124=0.8\times\text{black}$, so black $=155$. Black is $55\%$ faster than pink: $B=55$.

**Answer: 55**

Here $T=6$ comes from the previous question of the chain.
